issues.title: ICE: You can't project to field 0 of `DynMetadata` because layout is weird and thinks it doesn't have fields.

@rustbot label +F-ptr_metadata

processing.reason: The historical SRoA bug is a compile-time ICE during MIR validation, not a runtime miscompile. Before PR #125508, `escaping_locals` failed to exclude the fieldless-layout lang item `DynMetadata`, so `compute_flattening`/`iter_fields` projected to field 0 of `DynMetadata`; `-Zvalidate-mir` then rejected that MIR with "You can't project to field 0 of `DynMetadata` because layout is weird and thinks it doesn't have fields." The added regression test (`tests/ui/mir/dyn_metadata_sroa.rs`) only checks that compilation succeeds with `-Zmir-opt-level=5 -Zvalidate-mir`; it makes no runtime value assertion and there is no defined runtime value produced by the invalid projection. Modeling this in ordinary stable Rust would require either a different user-defined struct with real accessible fields (which is not `DynMetadata` and would not reproduce the historical transformation) or an unsupported/private/UB projection/transmute into `DynMetadata`'s implementation detail, which Miri would not accept as a defined execution. Therefore there is no source-grounded original/transformed function pair with identical inputs that both pass Miri and yield different defined runtime values; manufacturing one would test an unrelated rewrite rather than this ICE.

analysis.originalLogic: In `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/sroa.rs`, `escaping_locals` decides which locals SRoA must leave intact. It returns `true` (escaping) for excluded ADTs, including SIMD types, then otherwise assumes a non-union/non-enum ADT has a normal variant layout and proceeds to expose/split its fields. The surrounding logic states: "Exclude #[repr(simd)] types so that they are not de-optimized into an array" and "We already excluded unions and enums, so this ADT must have one variant".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Before the fix, SRoA did not exclude `DynMetadata` from aggregate replacement. It therefore treated a `DynMetadata<T>` local like an ordinary single-variant ADT and projected into its first field, even though the layout of `DynMetadata` reports no fields. MIR validation then failed: "You can't project to field 0 of `DynMetadata` because layout is weird and thinks it doesn't have fields." The correction is to make `DynMetadata` escape SRoA by comparing `Some(def.did()) == tcx.lang_items().dyn_metadata()` and returning `true`, because as the code comment says, "codegen wants to see the `DynMetadata<T>`, not the inner reference-to-opaque-type."
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR optimization at high MIR opt levels, especially `-Zmir-opt-level=5` with `-Zvalidate-mir`, for code using the unstable `ptr_metadata` feature and trait-object raw parts, e.g. `let a: *mut dyn Foo = &mut Bar; let d = a.to_raw_parts().0 as usize;`. The relevant type is `DynMetadata<T>` reached through `to_raw_parts()`.
analysis.summary: Historical bug fix: SRoA must treat `DynMetadata` as escaping and must not split/project into it. The original pass assumed non-union/non-enum ADTs have ordinary fields, but `DynMetadata` has a special layout with no fields; projecting to field 0 produced invalid MIR after `ScalarReplacementOfAggregates`.
analysis.trigger: A `DynMetadata<T>` value is present in MIR and SRoA is enabled (e.g. `-Zmir-opt-level=5`), such as when calling `to_raw_parts()` on a `*mut dyn Trait` and using the metadata component.
preconditions: Use a trait object raw-parts operation that produces or consumes `DynMetadata<T>`
Validate MIR with `-Zvalidate-mir` to expose invalid field projections
pitfalls: Do not treat every non-union/non-enum ADT as having accessible variant fields; `DynMetadata` has special layout and is reported as fieldless.
Do not split `DynMetadata` into its inner reference-to-opaque-type: codegen requires the `DynMetadata<T>` itself.
The failure is a compiler ICE during MIR validation, not a runtime miscompile; a run-pass test alone without `-Zvalidate-mir` may not exercise the validation failure.
The SIMD exclusion is a separate exclusion; fixing `DynMetadata` should not be generalized into a claim that all ADT field splitting is invalid.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `run-pass` UI test with `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-opt-level=5 -Zvalidate-mir`, `#![feature(ptr_metadata)]`, a simple trait and implementor, then `let a: *mut dyn Foo = &mut Bar; let _d = a.to_raw_parts().0 as usize;`. This drives `DynMetadata` through SRoA while MIR validation checks that SRoA did not create an invalid projection. The test comment should identify it as a regression for issue 125506 and note that it failed because SRoA projected into `DynMetadata`.
